guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Use red-green-refactor TDD and observe each required negative scenario fail before changing production behavior.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: The initial missing persist_activation ImportError and later v1 activated-state and second-staging-temp failures were observed before their production fixes; focused regressions now pass.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Keep fail-closed checks in CalibrationSession so direct CLI and Wizard cannot diverge.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: The Wizard delegates recording, preparation, confirmation, checks, and activation to CalibrationSession and persist_activation; direct CLI and Wizard regressions exercise the same blockers.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Use canonical JSON bytes for Candidate SHA-256 and never accept a confirmation that omits or mismatches the visible revision and digest.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: prepare_candidate hashes sorted compact UTF-8 JSON and confirm requires exact current revision and digest; mismatch and post-confirmation mutation regressions pass.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Preserve original path bytes before a two-file activation transaction and report rollback failure without claiming consistency.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: persist_activation captures bytes/existence before staging, restores attempted paths on failure, deletes initially absent paths, and emits consistency is unproved if rollback cannot be proved.

guidelinesCompliance.guideline: Keep English, Chinese, and Japanese semantics aligned and do not promote phase records to trusted actor identity evidence.
guidelinesCompliance.evidence: English, Chinese, and Japanese installation guides use common machine-checked markers and runtime terms while explicitly retaining the external actor-identity boundary.

risk.detail: Calibration activation writes authority-bearing repository state. The implementation therefore uses exact Candidate binding, fail-closed migration, and byte-restoring rollback rather than weakening the boundary.

observedIssues.fact: The first focused collection failed because the designed shared persist_activation transaction did not exist.
observedIssues.decision: Keep activation authority in one core helper shared by the direct CLI and Wizard.
observedIssues.resolution: Implemented persist_activation and covered success plus Active, Session, staging, absent-file, and rollback failures.
observedIssues.followUp: Require full quality and Hosted CI before considering the helper complete.

observedIssues.fact: An early schema v1 migration retained activated state even though legacy confirmations were not Candidate-bound.
observedIssues.decision: Never preserve unbound historical authority as current authorization.
observedIssues.resolution: Migration now moves old phase records to legacyConfirmationHistory, clears current confirmations and Candidate, and converts legacy activated state to paused/unverified.

observedIssues.fact: An early two-file staging path could leave the first temporary file behind if staging the second file failed.
observedIssues.decision: Treat staging cleanup as part of the transaction boundary.
observedIssues.resolution: The helper now cleans every staged temporary path before propagating failure and does not mutate Session authority before both replacements succeed.

observedIssues.fact: Marker-only installation checks could pass after deleting critical runtime terms from the prose.
observedIssues.decision: Require executable command and STOP terms in every language in addition to semantic markers.
observedIssues.resolution: check_docs_metadata.py now requires record-evidence, prepare-candidate, and consistency unproved in all three guides, with mutation regression.
observedIssues.followUp: Retain machine-checked runtime terms during later documentation alignment.

observedIssues.fact: Final reverse review found that the three guides' earlier Current implementation boundary still claimed Unknown was not machine-blocked and confirmations were not Candidate-bound, contradicting their newly aligned activation sections.
observedIssues.decision: Stop finish, replace all three stale boundary sections with current runtime facts, and make the obsolete marker itself forbidden.
observedIssues.resolution: English, Chinese, and Japanese now state the same enforced Unknown/incomplete/STOP and exact Candidate identity rules; a mutation regression rejects reintroduction of the obsolete boundary.
observedIssues.followUp: Re-run all focused documentation/calibration tests, quality-fast, and full ai-finish after this correction.

observedIssues.fact: The post-correction quality-fast run stopped before policy and heavy tests because Ruff required formatting scripts/check_docs_metadata.py and tests/test_docs_metadata.py.
observedIssues.decision: Keep formatter-first fail-fast behavior, format only the two named files, and rerun focused tests plus quality-fast from the beginning.
observedIssues.resolution: Ruff formatted the two files and git diff --check passed.
observedIssues.followUp: Require the replacement quality-fast and full ai-finish to pass.
